facts.fact: ANSSI CI announced on 24 July 2026 that the national public key infrastructure (PKI) is in service, at the top of the issuing tree for electronic certificates.
ANSSI CI states the national PKI is the trust base for all certification authorities operating in Cote d'Ivoire and supports the national electronic trust service providers.

CIV.note: The document says nothing about civil register and ID links.

facts.fact: ANSSI CI says the national PKI launch is part of implementing the National Cybersecurity Strategy and a 2026-2028 roadmap milestone of the digital ministry (MTNIT).

systems.country_label: Agence Nationale de Securite des Systemes d'Information

CIV.note: The PKI is called sovereign but no rule, hosting or contract terms for state data are stated.

facts.fact: ANSSI CI names Law No. 2013-546 of 30 July 2013 on electronic transactions as part of the regulatory framework in force that gives the electronic signature legal value.
ANSSI CI names Decree No. 2014-106 of 12 March 2014, setting the conditions for written records and electronic signature, and Decree No. 2014-105 on cryptology services, as rules under the framework.

CIV.note: No count of people holding a national ID is stated.
Nothing on a number at birth.
Nothing on who runs the national ID system.
No register keyed on the ID number is stated.
The national digital identity is only mentioned as something the PKI supports; no ID system is described.
ITU and ISO recognition of ANSSI CI as OID registration authority is neither standards body membership nor an adopted standard.
The document does not say who on staff runs or built the PKI.
